name: Mercado Central, Alicante (bombing of 25 May 1938)
story: At 11:18 on 25 May 1938, Italian Aviazione Legionaria SM.79 bombers flying from Mallorca dropped about 90 bombs on central Alicante. There were seven to nine aircraft, led by Captains De Prato and Zigiotti. The morning market was crowded and the sirens had not sounded. It was one of the deadliest air raids of the war on a purely civilian target, and together with raids on Granollers and on British ships it caused protests in London. The square in front of the market was renamed Plaza 25 de Mayo in 2010, and the city holds a memorial act every year.
see: A ceramic plaque on the market wall and nine aluminium plaques in the square, one for each aircraft, which glow red at noon for ten minutes. Inside, the siren and a clock stopped at the time of the attack are preserved.
plan: The market is open Monday to Saturday mornings; the plaques can be seen at any time. It pairs with the Séneca shelter, 10 minutes away on foot.

vis.label: Open
vis.text: Market: Mon–Fri 07:00–14:30; Sat and days before holidays 07:00–15:00

boxes.text: Death toll: the Republican war report gives 250, cemetery records about 275, the municipal plaque 311, and a Francoist document 393. More than 1,000 people were wounded.
